question: Vijay invests a sum of ₹5400 and Mohan invests a sum of ₹9400 at the same rate of simple interest per annum. If, at the end of 6 years, Mohan gets ₹600 more interest than Vijay, then find the rate of interest per annum (in percentage).
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Difference in principal amounts = ₹9400 − ₹5400 = ₹4000

Difference in simple interest earned in 6 years = ₹600

Simple interest for 1 year on the extra principal = ₹600 ÷ 6 = ₹100

Rate of interest = (100 ÷ 4000) × 100 = 2.5%

**∴ The correct answer is 2.5%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Vijay's Principal (P₁) = ₹5400

Mohan's Principal (P₂) = ₹9400

Time (T) = 6 years

Difference in Simple Interest = ₹600

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 
 Time (T) = 6 years, Rate (R) = ?

 
 
 Vijay
 P = ₹5400
 SI = I

 
 
 Mohan
 P = ₹9400
 SI = I + ₹600

 
 
• 
 

 ΔP = ₹4000
 ΔSI = ₹600

 
 Interest on extra ₹4000 in 6 years = ₹600
 1 year Interest = ₹100 → Rate = 2.5%

**Calculations:**

⇒ Mohan's SI − Vijay's SI = 600

⇒ (9400 × R × 6) ÷ 100 − (5400 × R × 6) ÷ 100 = 600

⇒ (56400R − 32400R) ÷ 100 = 600

⇒ 564R − 324R = 600

⇒ 240R = 600

⇒ R = 600 ÷ 240

⇒ R = 2.5%

**∴ The correct answer is 2.5%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Difference in Simple Interest

When the rate of interest (R) and the time period (T) are the same, the difference in interest earned is directly proportional to the difference in the principal amounts. Formula: ΔSI = (ΔP × R × T) ÷ 100.

Rate of Interest Definition

The rate of interest per annum defines the money earned on an investment of ₹100 in exactly one year.
